title: Technology Risk Director (Hybrid)
description: At Broadridge, we've built a culture where the highest goal is to empower others to accomplish more. If you’re passionate about developing your career, while helping others along the way, come join the Broadridge team. Broadridge is seeking a Technology Risk Director to join our growing Technology Risk organization. This role will support the identification, assessment, monitoring, and reporting of technology risks across infrastructure, cloud platforms, applications, cybersecurity, data, and emerging technologies. The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical background combined with a risk management mindset and an understanding of modern technology environments. The role requires close collaboration with engineering, infrastructure, cybersecurity, architecture, and business teams to ensure technology risks are effectively identified, assessed, and managed. Responsibilities Technology Risk Management Conduct technology risk assessments across infrastructure, applications, cloud platforms, and technology services. Identify technology risks, control gaps, and potential business impacts. Evaluate inherent and residual risks and support risk treatment planning. Monitor and track technology risk remediation activities through closure. Support Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) and technology risk governance activities. Technology Governance & Risk Oversight Partner with technology teams to ensure risks are appropriately identified, documented, and managed. Review new technology initiatives, architecture changes, and strategic programs from a risk perspective. Provide effective challenge and independent risk perspectives on technology decisions. Support the development and maintenance of technology risk policies, standards, and governance processes. Cloud, Infrastructure & Application Risk Assess risks associated with cloud environments, infrastructure platforms, applications, and technology operations. Review identity and access management, resilience, availability, data protection, and security controls from a risk perspective. Evaluate risks associated with modern architectures including APIs, microservices, containers, and cloud-native platforms. Support technology resilience and recovery risk assessments. Emerging Technology & AI Risk Support governance and risk assessments for Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI solutions. Evaluate risks related to data privacy, model governance, explainability, security, and responsible AI practices. Monitor emerging technology trends and assess associated risk implications. Assist in developing risk management approaches for emerging technologies and innovation initiatives. Automation & Continuous Risk Monitoring Leverage automation and analytics to improve technology risk identification and monitoring. Develop dashboards, reporting, and risk metrics using tools such as Python, SQL, Power BI, or similar technologies. Support continuous monitoring capabilities for key technology risk indicators. Identify opportunities to streamline risk processes through automation and AI-enabled solutions. Risk Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement Prepare risk reports, dashboards, and management presentations. Support development of Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and technology risk metrics. Communicate technology risks clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Partner with global technology, cybersecurity, compliance, and enterprise risk teams. Qualifications 5+ years of experience in Technology Risk, Information Security, Technology Governance, Cyber Risk, Cloud Risk, Infrastructure Engineering, Technology Operations, or related disciplines. Experience working within large-scale enterprise technology environments. Experience assessing risks associated with cloud, infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, or technology transformation initiatives. Technical Knowledge Strong understanding of several of the following areas: Cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) Infrastructure and platform technologies Identity and Access Management (IAM) Cybersecurity principles and controls Networking and distributed systems Application development and SDLC DevOps and CI/CD practices Databases and data management Technology resilience and disaster recovery APIs, containers, and microservices architectures Automation & Analytics Experience with one or more of the following: Python SQL Power BI Power Automate Tableau Data analytics and reporting platforms AI & Emerging Technology Knowledge Understanding of Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI technologies. Knowledge of AI governance, responsible AI principles, and technology risk implications. Awareness of emerging technology trends and associated risk management considerations. Frameworks & Standards Familiarity with technology risk and cybersecurity frameworks such as: NIST Cybersecurity Framework NIST AI Risk Management Framework COBIT CIS Controls FFIEC Technology Risk Guidance ISO 27001 Certifications (Preferred) One or more

title: Director, Data Governance (REMOTE, WA)
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role Are you a curious builder who thrives in a fast-moving, data-driven execution role, curious about how AI can turn quality data into real, operational trust? Veeam's business runs on data flowing from four source systems, v-Power for Sales, Marketo for Marketing, NetSuite for Finance, and Workday for HR, through a governed Databricks Lakehouse to certified outputs consumed by Tableau dashboards and AI agents. The Senior Director, AI-Ready Data Governance has authored the strategy for how this gets governed: a federated, pragmatic model, central standards, distributed ownership, sequenced by outcome so scope is committed on evidence rather than ambition. Continuous, agent-driven scoring keeps watching a certified object's quality on an ongoing basis, well past the moment of sign-off. This is a builder and execution role for a deep subject matter expert, with full autonomy to move fast and deliver results. You will lead highly complex, high-visibility initiatives, shape the approach to problems that arrive ambiguous, and influence organizational direction through the standards you set. The strategy, mission, and vision are set. The job is to run Databricks Unity Catalog as the technical backbone and Atlan as the business-facing catalog on top of it, build the certified Bronze-to-Silver-to-Gold pipeline domain by domain, and make certification, lineage, and continuous scoring real enough that governance becomes a standing rhythm rather than a one-off exercise. AI tooling is moving fast enough that the sequence of what gets built when will keep shifting. What does not shift is the outcome bar: certified data, a live trust score behind it, and a named owner for both. This is a job for someone who is curious by default. Someone who would rather have an agent draft the first pass of a lineage map than wait for a meeting about it, who gets energy from ambiguity because the pace of AI tooling means the plan will keep changing, and who treats data quality as something they are personally accountable for at every level, source system to dashboard to agent output, ahead of whatever a report tells them after the fact. What You’ll Do Run Databricks Unity Catalog and Atlan as the technical and business-facing backbone of certification, domain by domain Stand up continuous, agent-driven scoring behind certified data: a live trust score that keeps evaluating after certification, with an automated action attached to it Own the executive intelligence reporting that gives leadership a real, current answer to how much of Veeam's data can be trusted right now, and why Register and govern the AI agents that consume Veeam's data, and use agentic tools yourself, daily, to do the work faster. Align diverse business domain and data owners across Sales, Marketing, Finance, and HR on a defined set of standards. enterprise data governance, data management, or GTM Hands-on experience running enterprise data governance in production with a demonstrated track record driving a data and AI governance program end title: Security GRC Lead
description: ABOUT MERCOR Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices. ROLE DESCRIPTION You'll be the first GRC hire at a company that processes some of the most sensitive data on earth: training data, evals, and human-feedback pipelines for the frontier AI labs, plus payments and KYC for 300K+ experts. Compliance posture is a sales gate for every $50M+ contract Mercor signs. The audit calendar never ends. This is not an audit-theater role. You'll own the operating cadence of a continuously-audited company: continuous SOC 2 monitoring in Vanta, the active ISO 27001 buildout, an annual KPMG-style customer audit every quarter, and a sub-48-hour questionnaire SLA. You'll write controls in code where it makes sense, push back on tools that fight you, and own the artifacts that close enterprise deals. We use AI heavily in our own GRC work - Vanta has an MCP, our questionnaire bank is queryable, evidence is automated where the framework allows it. You should be comfortable using LLMs to draft, review, and respond at speed. If you've ever copy-pasted the same answer into 14 vendor questionnaires by hand, you'll appreciate not having to. We're in-person five days a week at our SF headquarters, with first Fridays remote. your call on sequencing) - A customer-audit machine that responds to Anthropic, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, and OpenAI without burning out the security team - questionnaire SLA under 48h, KPMG-grade evidence packs on demand - The third-party risk program - formal intake, recurring review cadence, evidence requirements - tied into procurement so vendors can't be onboarded around it - Policy lifecycle owned end-to-end: version, attestation, exception handling, review cycle - not a SharePoint graveyard - Controls-as-code where it makes sense: Vanta integrations, Wiz policy packs, Panther rules tied to SOC 2 CC categories, automated evidence collection - Data-handling procedures: the customer-data-deletion gap, DSAR workflow, KMS scheduled destruction, offboarding handlers - The internal trust narrative: customer trust pages, security one-pagers, executive-ready disclosure templates when something goes sideways WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 7+ years in security GRC, compliance engineering, or audit, with at least 2 years owning a SOC 2 Type 2 program end-to-end at a company under audit by enterprise customers - You've shipped at least one ISO 27001 certification from kickoff to issued certificate, including Stage 1 and Stage 2 with a real registrar - Fluent in Vanta (or Drata, Secureframe, Sprinto) at the integration and admin level, not just the reviewer UI - you've configured connectors, written custom tests, debugged broken evidence - You've sat on the company side of at least one enterprise customer audit conducted by a Big 4 firm (KPMG, EY, Deloitte, PwC) on behalf of a frontier customer - You translate cloud-security language to auditor language and back without losing precision - you can read a Wiz finding, a Panther rule, an IAM policy, and say what control it maps to - You write controls as code or query evidence with SQL when the platform falls short - Python, SQL, or shell, whatever it takes - You know the difference between "we don't have a control for that" and "we have a compensating control" and you don't fabricate the second one - Direct experience with the customer-trust surface: SIG, CAIQ, custom enterprise questionnaires, on-site auditor sessions, disclosure letters under legal review BONUS POINTS - title: Lead product manager
description: 🚀 About WRITER WRITER is where the world's leading enterprises orchestrate AI-powered work. Our vision is to expand human capacity through superintelligence. And we're proving it's possible – through powerful, trustworthy AI that unites IT and business teams together to unlock enterprise-wide transformation. With WRITER's end-to-end platform, hundreds of companies like Mars, Marriott, Uber, and Vanguard are building and deploying AI agents that are grounded in their company's data and fueled by WRITER's enterprise-grade LLMs. Valued at $1.9B and backed by industry-leading investors including Premji Invest, Radical Ventures, and ICONIQ Growth, WRITER is rapidly cementing its position as the leader in enterprise generative AI. Founded in 2020 with office hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Seattle, Austin, Chicago, and London, our team thinks big and moves fast, and we're looking for smart, hardworking builders and scalers to join us on our journey to create a better future of work with AI. 📐 About this role This is a chance to help shape the next chapter of WRITER's product at a moment when generative AI is redefining how work gets done. As senior staff product manager, you'll report directly to Wil Pong, VP of Product, and operate as a force-multiplier across the product organization — setting direction where it's unclear, aligning stakeholders, and making sure our most critical initiatives ship with excellence. You'll own ambiguous, high-impact problem spaces that span multiple product areas and teams, and you'll be equal parts strategist and operator. One moment you're shaping a multi-quarter roadmap; the next you're rolling up your sleeves to unblock execution. We're looking for someone who thrives at the intersection of customer empathy, technical depth, and business judgment — and who is energized by turning complex, evolving AI capabilities into products customers love. 🦸🏻‍♀️ Your responsibilities - Drive high-impact product initiatives end-to-end, from discovery and problem definition through launch, adoption, and iteration across areas that span multiple squads and surfaces - Shape product strategy and roadmap in partnership with the VP of Product and product leadership, translating company-level goals into clear, sequenced, ambitious bets - Spend time with enterprise buyers, end users, and prospects to uncover unmet needs, validate problem-solution fit, and champion the customer voice in every decision - Partner closely with engineering and design to define requirements, navigate technical tradeoffs, and build the right things in the right order, bringing real fluency to conversations about LLMs, agents, platform architecture, and data - Align cross-functional stakeholders across go-to-market, sales, marketing, customer success, and executive leadership, communicating strategy and tradeoffs with crisp, audience-appropriate narrative - Define and own success metrics for your areas, using data and qualitative signal to evaluate impact, course-correct, and tell the story of outcomes to leadership - Raise the bar on product craft across the org by mentoring and coaching other PMs, modeling best practices, and strengthening a culture built on rigor, customer obsession, and velocity ⭐️ Is this you? - 8+ years of product management experience with a track record of owning and shipping complex, high-impact products, ideally in SaaS, platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML-driven environments - Senior- or staff-level experience operating autonomously across ambiguous, multi-team problem spaces and influencing outcomes well beyond your immediate team - Genuine customer obsession — you instinctively go to the customer, synthesize signal from noise, and design from a deep understanding of real workflows and pain points - Technical credibility to engage meaningfully with engineers and researchers on system design, LLM capabilities, data, and architecture, knowing when to go deep and when to defer to the experts - A blend of strong strategic thinking and relentless execution — you can set a compelling vision one moment and sweat the details of a release plan the next - Exceptional communication that you tailor for any audience, from a frontline engineer to the executive team, driving alignment without relying on org chart authority - A mentor's instinct and a builder's drive, with the data-informed, outcome-driven mindset to define success up front and move with the speed this environment demands Nice to haves - Experience building products powered by LLMs, generative AI, or large-scale AI/ML systems - Background in enterprise software, developer platforms, or developer-facing products - Familiarity with AI governance, guardrails, and the operational considerations of deploying AI in regulated or high-stakes environments 🍩 Benefits & perks (US Full-time employees) - Generous PTO, plus company holidays - Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family - Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks) - F
